# The live updates example still sets its own gridline step

Owned: the post-merge item of PR #21740, done the hour both PRs landed; not offered to contributors.

## Context

PR #21740 (#21735) made the timeline draw one body gridline per header tick: the column writes the step inline on each track, and five examples dropped their hand-set steps. `examples/scheduler/liveUpdates` (PR #21694) was not on `dev` then, and both PRs named its rules as a follow-up once both merged. Both are on `dev` now (`cca960d9cd`, `eccf1a1749`).

## The Problem

`resources/css/src/examples/scheduler/liveUpdates/Viewport.css` still sets `--neo-timeline-gridline-step` four times: on `.gate-viewport` and on `.gate-scheduler .neo-timeline-track`, at 270 px, and both again at 180 px under `.is-compact`. None of them takes effect any more, and an example is code readers copy.

## The Architectural Reality

Design authority: "One gridline per tick: ticks start at the axis' start, as the gradient does." (`src/timeline/Column.mjs`, where the track's style is built).

- `Neo.timeline.Column` puts `--neo-timeline-gridline-step` in each `.neo-timeline-track`'s inline style whenever the axis has a fixed tick size, and an inline declaration beats both stylesheet rules.
- The track's gradient in `resources/css/src/timeline/Column.css` is the property's only reader, so the two viewport-level declarations reach nothing either.
- The example's axis ticks by the hour (`tickUnit: 'hour'`), so the inline step always applies; 270 px and 180 px were its tick sizes at its two `pxPerMinute` values.

## The Fix

Delete the four declarations (the two track rules and the two viewport properties). Add `scheduler/liveUpdates` to the examples `test/playwright/e2e/timeline/Gridlines.spec.mjs` measures, so its step stays equal to its tick at 1440 × 900 and 390 × 844.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The example's stylesheet sets no `--neo-timeline-gridline-step`.
- [ ] `Gridlines.spec.mjs` covers `scheduler/liveUpdates` at both widths and passes.

## Out of Scope

- The step for month ticks, which differ in length and keep the theme's step (`Column.mjs`).
- Any other rule of the example.

## Related

#21735 / PR #21740 (the axis-owned step) · #21621 / PR #21694 (the example).
